title: Tiered response contracts and traffic commit gates for progressive rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context:
We need a practical PRD that defines multi-tiered response contracts (latency envelopes, availability targets, and error-budget policies) and the automated gates that control progressive traffic commits during model or runtime rollouts. This ticket stitches together acceptance criteria, monitoring probes, and abort/rollback conditions so engineering teams can implement deterministic rollout automation in the Console and Orchestrator layers.

Goals:
- Define 3 latency envelopes (Gold / Silver / Bronze) with percentile bands and allowed degradation during canaries and staged ramp.
- Specify availability SLO and monthly error budget accounting per product tier and per-tenant where applicable.
- Define automated traffic commit gates (probe thresholds, burn-rate windows, and ramp percentages) and human escalation rules.
- Capture edge cases (burst traffic, regional failovers, model fallback cascades) and trade-offs between strict SLOs and progressive rollout velocity.
acceptance_criteria: Numeric SLOs defined and published in the SLO registry and surfaced in Console.
Rollout engine enforces canary size/ramp steps and evaluates the defined gates automatically.
Gate trip results in automated hold/soft-rollback with audit logging and on-call notification.
Synthetic probe harness and dashboards show green for staging runs under simulated faults.
Integration test coverage for gating logic with injected latency and error scenarios.

slo_targets: Gold: availability >= 99.95% monthly; p50 < 30ms; p95 < 120ms; p99 < 350ms; error budget = 0.05% of requests per month.
Silver: availability >= 99.9% monthly; p50 < 50ms; p95 < 200ms; p99 < 500ms; error budget = 0.1% per month.
Bronze: availability >= 99.5% monthly; p50 < 100ms; p95 < 400ms; p99 < 800ms; error budget = 0.5% per month.
rollout_recipe: Baseline: rolling baseline measured from previous stable release (30m window).
Canary: 5% sampled traffic for 10m evaluation window. If gates pass, ramp to 20% and evaluate 15m, then 50% (20m), then 100% (30m).
Probe checks: per-window checks for request success rate, p95/p99 deltas, and error-budget burn. Each check reports pass/warn/fail. A single fail leads to an automated hold and a soft-rollback.
Human override: SRE/PM can manually force continue with documented justification; records audit event and requires postmortem within 72h if issues occur.
gate_examples: Immediate abort if request success rate drops by >1.5 percentage points relative to baseline AND absolute errors increase by >50 requests/min for a 5m window.
Abort if p99 latency in canary cohort exceeds baseline p99 by >25% for two consecutive 5m windows.
Abort if error-budget burn rate > 4x sustained for 10m.
